scope: Shared Linux ARM64 development workspace, native executables and libraries, and MAP_PRIVATE data. MAP_SHARED is explicitly unsupported.

environment.executor: HVF ARM64 with the common userspace Linux kernel

tools.layout: Linux /usr and /lib mounted read-only from a prepared native tools tree; /work mounted read/write. This is not the Mac host system tree.

implementation: Private host-file pages retain the original native FD and read only on first reach through the existing shared guest page/COW model.
Private map snapshots never replace the ordinary inode I/O cache, so normal reads continue to observe native edits.
Guest-known length changes update EOF metadata through relaxed scalar generations, including after private COW.
Initial session launch and execve/execveat share one bounded shebang parser.
Executable capabilities retain their native inode across host atomic replacement.
Create/open preserves the creation FD when mode bits are already read-only, fixing Git object creation without changing permissions.
Weak per-access handle registrations preserve older open files after the newest handle closes, without retaining one FD per cached closed inode.

compatibility: Final iPad optional hostfs compile check
validation.build: Final normal Mac bundle build, signing and strict signature verification passed.
new_unit_coverage: Lazy private pages and guest COW leave native data unchanged, including a 4 KiB file offset on the 16 KiB-page Mac.
Native edits remain visible through normal pread after a private page becomes resident.
Original native inode survives atomic replacement and descriptor close for exec and mapping.
Partial final page is zero-filled; a past-EOF page faults; guest truncation invalidates even an existing private COW page.
Creating a 0444 file keeps its original writable FD.
Closing the latest same-access native handle retains earlier open-unlinked descriptions.
Shared shebang parser covers CRLF, optional argument grouping and invalid/oversized headers.
validation.unchanged_results_reused: No repeat of unchanged CPU, network, graphics or full I/O throughput acceptance.

limits: All host MAP_SHARED mappings return ENODEV; SQLite WAL probe currently fails with a disk I/O error.
Resident private mapped pages are snapshots and do not monitor external host edits/truncation; remap when coordinating such changes.
Host edit inotify, native-writer advisory lock coordination, xattrs and special host files remain unsupported.
Programs must use the Linux ARM64 ABI; macOS Mach-O binaries are not Linux programs.
The ordinary rootfs importer remains a bounded minimal-bootstrap importer; no size limits were raised for tool fixtures.
